# template-manifest.txt — which paths the template manages in YOUR office
#
# The factory-update workflow syncs ONLY the paths listed here from the
# template (squidbay/factory) into your office, always as a pull request
# you review and merge. Anything NOT listed is yours alone and is never
# touched: your journal, your specs, your roster in FACTORY.md, any
# mission packs you added, and this repo's own denylist.
#
# One path per line. A trailing slash means "the whole folder."
# Lines starting with # are comments.
#
# Your office's copy of this file governs — to opt a path out of updates,
# remove its line here (the update PR may propose restoring it; declining
# that hunk is your call and the workflow respects the merged result).
#
# A line starting with "!" PROTECTS a path: the sync will never write it,
# even though it sits under a managed folder listed below. Use it for a file
# this office has deliberately made its own and does not want the template to
# reclaim. Same shape as the rest — a trailing slash protects a whole folder.
#
# Two things the sync can never do to you:
#   • It never DELETES. A file of yours the template has never heard of is
#     left alone, not removed. (An earlier version `rm -rf`'d each managed
#     folder and re-copied it, which silently deleted every office-only file
#     inside.)
#   • It never writes a "!" path. Overwrite is still how updates arrive for
#     everything else — "!" is how you say "not this one."

CLAUDE.md
FROM-HQ.md
MECHANICAL-RULES.md
README.md
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
VERSIONS.md
.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
.github/SECURITY.md
.github/template-version.txt

# The updater's own engine. .github/workflows/factory-update.yml EXECUTES
# scripts/factory-sync.sh (the copying) and scripts/sync-selftest.sh (the proof,
# run before every sync). The workflow and the code it runs are ONE subsystem:
# if the scripts are not managed, a fix to the sync engine lands upstream and
# stops at your door in silence, while your workflow keeps running the old one.
# Managed here so the two can never drift apart.
scripts/
grounding/
guides/
hosting/
inbox/drop/README.md
journal/README.md
missions/README.md
missions/design-guide/
missions/first-app/
missions/first-website/
missions/organize-my-business/
missions/website-overhaul/
onboarding/
seats/
specialists/
specs/README.md
skills/factory-coach/
skills/factory-render-verify/
skills/factory-retro/
skills/factory-security/
skills/factory-update/
skills/skill-creator/
skills/README.md
templates/
tokens/
versions/

# Deliberately absent — user-owned, never synced:
#   FACTORY.md            (carries your roster and your names)
#   journal.md            (your team's memory — HQ's own news rides the
#                          managed FROM-HQ.md instead, never journal.md)
#   journal/archive/      (your history)
#   specs/                (your plans; only its README is managed)
#   .github/guardrails-denylist.txt  (your private-name denylist)
#   .github/heartbeat-watch.txt      (your own nightly watch list)
#   .github/workflows/    (a repo's automation can't be rewritten by its
#                          own automation — workflow changes arrive as a
#                          note in the update PR for a Code seat to apply.
#                          This is the ONE part of the updater that cannot be
#                          synced. Its engine, scripts/, is managed above, so
#                          the hand-carry is the workflow file alone — and
#                          guides/SAFE-UPDATE-BOOTSTRAP.md is the order to do
#                          it in, for an office that still has the old one.)
